Getting started with quorum

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(quorum)

Why

quorum compares lenses, but a lens has to exist before it can be compared. The question this vignette answers is the one an analyst asks before any comparison is possible: I have an APSIM ensemble, a cheap emulator I would rather use than the simulator itself, and a koine pass – none of them came out of a flexyBayes fit, so how does each become something quorum can even read? The three seams below are the three answers, one on-ramp each.

What

A quorum_lens() compares two things that agree on their shape: two sets of parameter draws, or two response curves over the same grid. An APSIM ensemble, a surrogate’s predictive distribution and a koine fit each start in a different shape of their own, so each needs its own on-ramp into the lens vocabulary. fb_ensemble() and verify_fb_ensemble() are the ensemble on-ramp (contract C5): they canonicalise and check a set of parameter draws paired with a simulator’s response, whatever produced it. fit_surrogate() is the surrogate on-ramp (contract C7): it trains a fast, distribution-preserving stand-in for an expensive simulator, so a mechanism lens does not have to pay the simulator’s cost on every draw. emit_koine() and koine_status() are the koine on-ramp (contract C3): koine’s own battery battery, wrapped so its opinion reaches the same canonical parameter names a hub fit uses. None of the three verbs below builds or compares a lens directly – that is A quorum of lenses on Study A0 and Adding a lens’s job – this vignette only gets each estimate through its own door.

Do

Seam 1 – ingest a simulation ensemble (contract C5)

A simulation ensemble is a set of parameter draws paired with the simulator’s response to each draw: a design matrix and a row-aligned output matrix. fb_ensemble() is the canonical container; as_fb_ensemble() (not called directly here) coerces a conforming producer – a PESTO calibration manifest, a raw apsimx run, a saved file – into that same shape, so a mechanism lens never has to know which producer it came from. The parameter-to-output map below is synthetic, standing in for whatever an APSIM run would have produced.

set.seed(20260902)
g <- rbind(c(1.5, -0.8), c(0.4, 1.1)) # 2 outputs x 2 params, for illustration
theta <- cbind(p1 = runif(80, -2, 2), p2 = runif(80, -2, 2))
y <- theta %*% t(g) + matrix(rnorm(160, 0, 0.1), 80, 2L)
colnames(y) <- c("o1", "o2")

ens <- fb_ensemble(
  params = as.data.frame(theta),
  outputs = as.data.frame(y),
  provenance = list(source = "raw")
)
verify_fb_ensemble(ens)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] ""

verify_fb_ensemble() is the conformance check: it fails loudly, naming the first violation, rather than letting a malformed ensemble reach a surrogate fit silently.

Seam 2 – emulate the simulator (contract C7)

fit_surrogate() trains a fast stand-in for the simulator: a map from parameters to outputs that reports a predictive distribution, not a point, so a downstream calibration step can account for emulator error instead of treating the surrogate as exact. The reference method, "rff", is a random-features Bayesian linear model. Writing ϕ(x)∈ℝm\phi(x) \in \mathbb{R}^m for the random Fourier feature map of a parameter vector xx (Rahimi and Recht, 2007), the predictive distribution at a new point x*x_* is Gaussian with

𝔼[y∣x*]=ϕ(x*)⊤μN,Var⁡[y∣x*]=1t+ϕ(x*)⊤SNϕ(x*), \mathbb{E}[y \mid x_*] = \phi(x_*)^{\top} \mu_N, \qquad \operatorname{Var}[y \mid x_*] = \frac{1}{t} + \phi(x_*)^{\top} S_N \, \phi(x_*),

where μN\mu_N and SNS_N are the posterior mean and covariance of the linear weights and tt is the noise precision; both the prior precision aa and tt are set by MacKay evidence maximisation rather than fixed by hand (Bishop, 2006, secs. 3.3, 3.5). That evidence-optimised tt is what makes the reported standard deviation calibrated instead of an arbitrary ridge parameter.

sur <- fit_surrogate(ens)
pred_point <- predict(sur, data.frame(p1 = 1, p2 = -1))
Predictive mean and SD at (p1, p2) = (1, -1).
o1_mean o1_sd o2_mean o2_sd
o1 2.296 0.159 -0.704 0.162 
p2_fixed <- mean(theta[, "p2"])
sweep_grid <- data.frame(p1 = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 100L), p2 = p2_fixed)
pred_sweep <- predict(sur, sweep_grid)
band_df <- data.frame(
  p1 = sweep_grid$p1,
  mean = pred_sweep$o1_mean,
  lo = pred_sweep$o1_mean - 2 * pred_sweep$o1_sd,
  hi = pred_sweep$o1_mean + 2 * pred_sweep$o1_sd
)
ens_df <- data.frame(p1 = theta[, "p1"], o1 = y[, "o1"])

ggplot2::ggplot(band_df, ggplot2::aes(x = p1)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "#440154", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = mean), colour = "#440154",
                     linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = ens_df, ggplot2::aes(x = p1, y = o1), colour = "#21908C",
    alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "p1 (p2 fixed at its ensemble mean)", y = "o1",
    title = "The surrogate against the ensemble it emulates"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

The surrogate’s predictive mean and +/- 2 SD band as p1 sweeps with p2 fixed at its ensemble mean (line and ribbon), against the ensemble’s own training outputs for o1 (points). The surrogate never sees the points directly at predict time – it interpolates the distribution it was fitted to.

Richer emulators – PESTO’s Gaussian process, kernR’s conditional mean embedding – register through register_surrogate() and are consumed through exactly this same predict() contract; see Distribution-preserving surrogates for the full loop, including inversion against observed data and a posterior-predictive check of whether the surrogate distorted the output distribution.

Seam 3 – triangulate with koine (contract C3)

koine is a stacked battery of marginal-likelihood and robust lenses, wrapped so its opinion reaches the hub’s own canonical parameter names – an independently-derived fourth opinion that lens_koine() (see Adding a lens) reaches directly, and that flexyBayes::triangulate() compares against the Bayesian backends inside the hub itself. emit_koine() carries the model into koine’s own corner: a population GLM with either a single random intercept or – from koine 0.3.0 – the multi-environment-trial structure of two crossed or nested random intercepts, (1 | variety) + (1 | trial), which is the shape a variety trial actually has. Anything richer returns a typed abstention rather than a wrong fourth opinion. koine_status() reports whether the slot is currently active on the installed koine version, without requiring koine to be installed to load this package:

status <- koine_status()
status$activated
#> [1] TRUE

Read

The predictive table above reports the surrogate’s mean and SD at one point; both are finite and the SD is strictly positive, which is what a distribution-preserving prediction requires – a surrogate that reported zero uncertainty anywhere inside its design would be silently claiming certainty the training ensemble does not support. The figure shows the same thing across a sweep: the band tracks the scatter of training points, widening only where the points themselves thin out. status$activated reports TRUE on this build, meaning the koine fourth opinion is live and emit_koine() will attempt a real fit rather than decline outright; a build without a compatible koine install would report FALSE here, and every claim in this vignette about koine would still hold as a description of the seam, just not as something this render exercised.

Limits

None of the three chunks above compares two lenses against each other – that comparison, and the independence and agreement machinery behind it, is what Adding a lens and A quorum of lenses on Study A0 exercise. The ensemble here is synthetic, standing in for an APSIM run so this vignette needs no external binary and no network call; a real ensemble carries the same shape but a different, and generally larger, predictive uncertainty once the surrogate has to interpolate a genuinely nonlinear response rather than the near-linear toy used here.

What to read next

Distribution-preserving surrogates walks the full seam-2 loop end to end – ingest, fit, read the distribution, invert, and check – on a small worked example with figures. A quorum of lenses on Study A0 and Adding a lens pick up where this vignette stops: turning an ingested estimate into a lens and comparing it against another. ?fit_surrogate, ?fb_surrogate_ies, and ?fb_surrogate_ppc document each verb’s arguments and return value.
